physical_visual_observation.initial_release: At frame 0 the red floating body is visibly separated from the blue initial fluid surface within the tank; the tank, fluid, and body are all present in the native-bounds views.
physical_visual_observation.early_release_to_impact: The early sequence around frames 30-60 shows fluid rise/splash around the body and body-fluid contact. This is recorded as the visible release/impact event; contact at the fluid interface is not called numerical penetration.
physical_visual_observation.later_motion: Frames 90-240 show the body remaining inside the tank while its visible pose and immersion change as the fluid surface oscillation settles. The sequence is continuous from release through impact to later pose change.
physical_visual_observation.mechanism_statement: The reviewed images make the qualitative release -> early impact/splash -> later reorientation/settling sequence discernible. This is a visual sequence observation only and does not establish quantitative physical correctness.

gross_visual_screen.visual_scope: These are image-level observations; report metadata, not pixels, is the source for finite-state and frame-count claims.

uncertain_or_unclaimed: No final UID survival or particle-loss cause is inferred from the images; producer lifecycle metadata remains separate.
No quantitative angular-velocity, conservation, convergence, precision, Q-N/Q-E, or production claim is made.
The images do not by themselves prove the declared initial angular state or rule out sub-resolution contact errors.
The producer-reported missing events (933 cumulative, maximum 4 in one frame) are retained and are not converted into a final particle count.
